Senator Beebe-Center, Representative Hasenfus and honorable members of the Joint Standing Committee on Criminal Justice and Public Safety, I am Laurie Osher, and I represent House District 25, which is most of Orono. Thank you for the opportunity to come before you today to speak in opposition to LD 303, An Act to Repeal the Law Prohibiting Unauthorized Paramilitary Training.
The Maine Constitution explicitly states, "No standing army shall be kept up in time of peace without the consent of the Legislature, and the military shall, in all cases, and at all times, be in strict subordination to the civil power".

This bill seeks to repeal the statute created by LD 2130, An Act to Prohibit Unauthorized Paramilitary Training, that passed last year.

Prior to passing LD 2130, Act to Prohibit Unauthorized Paramilitary Training, our laws did not provide the power to Maine's law enforcement professionals to prevent people from engaging in paramilitary training here in Maine for the purpose of civil unrest.

I sponsored LD 2130 after a white supremacist leader from Ohio purchased property in Springfield, Maine, less than 60 miles from my district, and began a social media campaign to raise funds to build a paramilitary training facility there. That man sold the property after the significant public outcry and concern in response to his plans. His goal of training wannabe militia members "to prepare for a coming race war" highlighted the need for the Maine Legislature to clarify in statute that is allowed in Maine.

Our constitution explicitly prohibits armies that do not have consent of the Legislature, and out legislature has not called for a militia to be created.

The bill that I sponsored last session, LD 2130, passed both the House and Senate and was signed into law by Governor Janet Mills. It ensured such activity can be prevented and stopped.
The facility that was being planned in Springfield wasn't the only one.
